items.title: Continuous - dogfooding and evidence
items.description: Run the kit on its own work so first-use friction is discovered by its maintainers rather than by its first adopter.
acceptance_criteria: The kit's own roadmap is managed through the kit

items.title: Operations - release plumbing and cleanup
items.description: Release automation and disposable-resource cleanup. Excluded from the product completion basis: none of it changes what the kit does.
acceptance_criteria: Release automation is organization-managed and recoverable
No orphaned evaluation resources remain

items.title: Planning and handoff - leave a backlog another agent can pick up
items.description:
A backlog is used across sessions and across agents. Whoever arrives next did not watch the last one work, so what to do next has to be answerable from the repository rather than from memory or from prose somebody remembered to update.

This line covers what the kit must compute so prose does not have to: an auditable next selection, and a timeline projection of the work behind it.
acceptance_criteria: What to work on next is answerable by running the kit, with the reasoning visible
The backlog can be projected onto a timeline and rendered without adding a dependency
No tracked document restates a ranking the kit can compute

items.title: Unscheduled - portfolio scale
items.description: Work that is understood but deliberately not scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: Revisited only after the adoption line lands

items.title: v0.1.0 - Initial release
items.description: Ship a deterministic, installable plugin that reconciles a manifest with GitHub Issues and Projects.
acceptance_criteria: Published release with validated assets and green hosted CI

items.title: v0.1.1 - Engine correctness
items.description: Repair the defects found in the shipped deterministic engine.
acceptance_criteria: Deep dependency graphs resolve without recursion failure
Completed work scores zero and relays no boost

items.title: v0.1.2 - Apply ergonomics
items.description: First use of the kit on its own backlog showed that apply succeeds but does not explain itself: a failure names no item, and a completed scaffold can still leave the target unconverged.
acceptance_criteria: An apply failure names the item, the field, and the reason
One scaffold apply converges a fresh Project

items.title: v0.2.0 - GitHub operational authority
items.description: Let fresh GitHub operational state govern existing work instead of stale local intent. Policy D1 and carryover policy A are approved.
acceptance_criteria: Remote completion and assignment survive ordinary sync
Sprint commitments and carryover are explicit and reviewed

items.title: v0.3.0 - Adoption
items.description: Make the kit usable on a repository that already has a backlog.
acceptance_criteria: An existing repository can be imported without touching unselected issues

items.title: v0.4.0+ - Reconciliation and reach
items.description: Close the reconciliation gaps and settle the transport question.
acceptance_criteria: Removal and reverse-sync have explicit policy, preview, and recovery
The dedicated-MCP decision is recorded with evidence

items.title: Infer hierarchy and dependencies when importing existing issues
items.description:
Import (R11) adopts an existing issue with a neutral type, no parent and no dependencies.

GitHub already records sub-issue links and `blocked_by` dependencies for these issues, so an import preview could propose that structure rather than flattening it. It does not yet: every adopted item lands with `parent: null` and `depends_on: []`, and a human has to rebuild the shape by hand.

Reading it costs one extra request per issue for the parent and one for dependencies, which is why the first cut left it out. Worth revisiting once import has been used on a repository big enough to care.

Found while implementing R11 on 2026-09-19.

items.title: Make the Agentic Backlog Kit a finished product
items.description: Take the kit from a shipped v0.1.0 that only its author can use to a product another team can adopt on an existing repository.
acceptance_criteria: Every release line has an owner, a denominator, and a done definition
The kit manages its own backlog through its own workflows

items.title: R01 - Bind apply operations to fresh local and remote state
items.description: Sync, scaffold, and bootstrap plans bind normalized local and remote fingerprints with per-action preconditions, and apply aborts on drift.
acceptance_criteria: Drift aborts before the first write
Partial failure produces an auditable receipt

items.title: R02 - Run live GitHub end-to-end evaluations
items.description: Complete lifecycle evaluation against disposable repositories and organization Projects on every supported native transport.
acceptance_criteria: Each supported executor completes the workflow
The second plan contains zero actions

items.title: R03 - Complete first-run Project creation and discovery
items.description: init-plan discovers organization Projects by exact number, title, or unique repository association, and fails closed on ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: A user can start with only an organization and repository

items.title: R04 - Reconcile complete Project view configuration
items.description: Scaffold snapshots retain view identity, layout, filter, visible fields, grouping, and sorting; a same-name view is never accepted on name alone.
acceptance_criteria: Incorrect same-name views are detected and repair plans converge

items.title: R05 - Manage the iteration lifecycle
items.description: Full active and completed iteration definitions are canonical snapshot state; sprint planning resolves exact titles plus @current and @next.
acceptance_criteria: Missing iterations are handled through a reviewed plan

items.title: R06 - Evaluate the installed plugin and skill activation
items.description: The plugin was installed from a local marketplace and exercised through real conversations covering direct, indirect, negative, and write cases.
acceptance_criteria: The intended skill activates consistently
Unsupported requests do not activate it

items.title: R07 - Publish the repository, run Linux CI, and release 0.1.0
items.description: Public repository, hosted Linux CI, branch protection, tag, release assets, and clean public-checkout verification.
acceptance_criteria: Branch protection is active and the tag contains documented artifacts

items.title: R08 - Select a license and complete public-release documentation
items.description: Source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with a separate paid licence for for-profit operational use.
acceptance_criteria: Repository and package metadata agree
No unresolved legal or documentation placeholders

items.title: R09 - Measure and enforce token-efficiency targets
items.description: Deterministic 100, 1,000, and 10,000-item fixtures measure compact and pretty JSON for every model-facing operation, enforced in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Large-backlog benchmarks are repeatable
CI detects material output-size regressions

items.title: R10 - Close the work lifecycle from evidence
items.description: Synchronization was additive and update-only. Owner decision 2026-09-24: the lifecycle is automated from evidence, never from the manifest's silence. GitHub already closes an issue when a PR carrying `Closes #N` merges, and Project 6's built-in workflows mark it Done. The kit makes that reliable, finishes the loop for parents, removes relationships the manifest dropped, and treats Priority-only housekeeping as pre-authorized. It never closes, deletes, or archives an issue because the manifest no longer lists it.
acceptance_criteria: Agents following the kit's skills link every PR to its kit-managed issues with a closing keyword
A parent whose children are all closed is proposed for closure through plan, digest confirmation, apply, and receipt
A parent or dependency link the manifest no longer declares is proposed for removal through the same contract, with recovery information
A plan made only of Priority field updates is recognized mechanically and may be applied without a separate confirmation
No issue is closed, deleted, or archived because it is absent from the manifest

items.title: R11 - Import existing backlogs and support bulk ingestion
items.description: Ingestion handles one structured item at a time and only marked issues are managed, so the kit is usable only on a greenfield repository. This is the gate on adoption by anyone other than the maintainer.
acceptance_criteria: An existing repository imports without modifying unselected issues
Duplicate mappings are rejected
A second import is idempotent

items.title: R12 - Support multi-repository portfolio planning
items.description: One manifest targets one repository and one organization Project. Deliberately deferred until the adoption line lands.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple repositories participate in one portfolio without ID ambiguity

items.title: R13 - Complete native transport parity and decide on a dedicated MCP server
items.description: Authenticated gh and direct GraphQL are proven peers. The installed generic GitHub MCP lacks the Projects surface and fails capability preflight without writing.
acceptance_criteria: Every declared-compatible route produces equivalent plans and state
The dedicated-MCP decision is recorded with token and call evidence

items.title: R14 - Adopt organization-managed semantic releases
items.description: Version calculation, tagging, and Release creation are delegated to the reusable workflows in aegolius-labs/.github. Hosted no-bump and immutable publication passed; missing-baseline handling and recovery proof remain.
acceptance_criteria: The shared interface and caller pass permission and recovery tests
Hosted failure recovery after draft creation is proven

items.title: R15 - Respect GitHub operational status and sprint authority
items.description: Ordinary sync overwrites remote Status and Sprint with stale local intent, so remote completion and assignment are lost. Policy D1 is approved: fresh GitHub state governs existing work.
acceptance_criteria: Remote completion and assignment survive stale local intent
Planning uses fresh operational state
Explicit transitions fail safely on drift

items.title: R16 - Preserve sprint commitments and review carryover
items.description: Replanning must not move committed work automatically or regress status. Carryover policy A is approved: work assigned elsewhere is excluded from automatic selection and offered as explicit carryover.
acceptance_criteria: Replanning neither moves work automatically nor regresses status
Capacity, dependencies, overage, and carryover verify against fresh state

items.title: R17 - Support deep dependency graphs without recursion failure
items.description: Prioritization raised RecursionError from roughly 500 chained items and validation from roughly 1,200. Both traversals are now iterative and cycle diagnostics are bounded.
acceptance_criteria: 10,000-node forward and reverse chains validate and prioritize
Deep cycles are still detected and reported compactly
The benchmark report digest is unchanged

items.title: R18 - Enforce zero final scores for completed work
items.description: The dependency boost propagated into the final score of completed work, so a Done item with two dependents scored 4.0 instead of 0.0 and relayed a boost to its own prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria: Completed prerequisites score zero for default and custom done statuses
Unfinished graph scores and stable ordering are unchanged

items.title: R19 - Publish accurate release and remediation status
items.description: Public main documents the completed v0.1.0 release and the outstanding corrective work. Verified present on origin/main on 2026-09-18.
acceptance_criteria: Public main documents the release and outstanding work

items.title: R20 - Resolve remaining disposable evaluation resources
items.description: Fresh discovery on 2026-09-24 (S-R20-1) verified Project #4 absent and found five resources. Owner decision 2026-09-24: delete the two Wave C repositories, Project #5, and abk-adopt-eval-20260922; retain abk-release-eval-20260908 as the hosted release test bed.
acceptance_criteria: The four retired resources are verified absent
The release fixture's retention is recorded as an explicit election

items.title: R21 - Run the kit against its own backlog
items.description: The kit had never been pointed at its own work: zero issues, no manifest, no managed Project. This roadmap was maintained by hand in one large Markdown file - exactly the artifact the kit exists to manage.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked manifest describes the open roadmap
A scaffolded Project reflects it
A second sync plan contains zero actions
Friction is written up against the responsible work item

items.title: R22 - Report actionable apply failures
items.description: An apply failure surfaces as 'GitHub API error 1: gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422)', naming no item, field or reason. Diagnosis required reading the receipt, querying organization issue types by hand, and reading the transport source. The receipt is good; the operator-facing message is not.
acceptance_criteria: A failed action names the item id and the rejected field
A known cause such as an unavailable issue type is named explicitly
The remedy or the fallback taken is stated

items.title: R23 - Converge a fresh Project in one scaffold apply
items.description: project.view.create cannot carry a filter, visible fields, grouping or sorting, so every created view needs an immediate repair pass. The first apply reports completed with 17 of 17 actions while leaving three views unconverged; convergence arrives only on the third plan.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh Project converges in one reviewed apply, or the plan states plainly that a second pass is required
A completed status never implies a converged target when it is not

items.title: R24 - Reconsider hierarchy expressiveness for small work
items.description: The hierarchy is a strict ladder and a parent must be exactly one level above its child, so a small chore directly under a Feature has no type: Task is reserved for level 5 under a Story or Bug. Six decomposed items had to be retyped from Task to Story, which overstates them. This may be intentional; it is recorded rather than scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded either way, with the modeling rationale

items.title: R25 - Carry a canonical GUID through to GitHub for Seam A traceability
items.description:
The authority model in aio-agentic-sdlc requires that a canonical GUID be carried into the ABK item and into the GitHub issue body marker, so a projected issue can always be traced back to its Intention DAG node. This kit cannot do that: `$defs.item` sets `additionalProperties: false` over a fixed field list with no GUID field, and nothing writes or reads a second marker key.

Design approved by the owner on 2026-09-24: an optional item field `guid`, holding a canonical lowercase UUID exactly as aio-agentic-sdlc canonicalizes it (`str(UUID(value)) == value`). Manifest `schema_version` becomes 2 with a tested migration from 1. The marker gains `;guid=<uuid>` only on items that carry one and keeps `schema=1`, because older parsers read the id only up to the first `;` and existing issue bodies need no rewrite. A known limit to document: an older kit that rewrites a body drops the key.

This does not block standalone use, which is a supported configuration. It is a cost that grows with every issue created before the carrier exists.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest item can carry an optional canonical GUID without failing validation, under schema version 2 with a tested migration from version 1
A GUID that is not a canonical lowercase UUID is rejected before planning
The issue body marker carries the GUID when the item has one, and round-trips through read and adoption without loss
An item with no GUID stays valid and its marker is unchanged, because standalone use owns no Intention DAG
A Seam A fixture is committed here and its counterpart in aio-agentic-sdlc, so neither repository imports the other to test the contract

items.title: R26 - Make the next task answerable by the kit rather than by prose
items.description:
`next` returned one id and silently discarded everything ranked above it. Four separate conditions - a container type, completed status, an explicit block, and unrefined maturity - plus unmet dependencies each dropped an item with no record, so an operator who ran it saw an answer that looked wrong and could not tell why. It also defaults to local intent, which lags GitHub.

The cost was borne by the prose instead. Every activation checkpoint in docs/task-handoff.md restated a ranking by hand, and every one went stale; the 2026-09-22 checkpoint named an item that shipped the same day.

Found on 2026-09-22 while assessing whether this repository could be picked up by another agent.
acceptance_criteria: `next --explain N` reports the higher-ranked items it passed over, each with the reason it was not selectable
Completed work is not reported as an obstacle, because it is bookkeeping rather than something in the way
The existing `select_next` contract is unchanged for its callers
A tracked document states that a handoff may not restate anything the kit can compute

items.title: R27 - Project the backlog onto a timeline and render a Gantt chart
items.description:
The manifest carries effort, a proven-acyclic dependency graph, computed priority and an iteration start date - everything a schedule needs - and the kit could not draw one. Sequence over time had to be reconstructed by hand from `prioritize` output, which is exactly the hand-maintained artifact this kit exists to replace.

The projection must stay honest. Effort points are an ordinal scale, so converting them to duration is a declared convention rather than a measurement, and the chart has to say so rather than read as a delivery date.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic schedule places every schedulable item after the dependencies it declares
Concurrency is explicit and never reorders a dependency
Containers and completed work are excluded with their reasons rather than silently dropped
Rendering adds no runtime dependency and renders where the backlog already lives
Every chart states its duration basis, its lane count, and that it is a projection rather than an estimate
A committed projection is regenerable and a test fails when it no longer matches the manifest

items.title: Make agents link PRs to kit issues with closing keywords
items.description: GitHub closes an issue when a PR carrying `Closes #N` merges, and Project 6 marks it Done. Today that depends on habit: no skill tells an agent to do it. Make it part of the kit's guidance so evidence-based closure is dependable.
acceptance_criteria: The skills that hand work to an agent instruct it to put a closing keyword for each kit-managed issue a PR completes
The guidance says not to close a parent this way unless the PR completes the parent's acceptance criteria

items.title: Propose closing a parent once every child is closed
items.description: A Feature whose Stories all closed stays open until someone remembers it; R21 sat that way. Closing it is supported by evidence, the children's closure, so the kit may propose it. It still goes through plan, digest confirmation, apply, and receipt.
acceptance_criteria: A sync plan proposes closing and marking Done a parent whose children are all closed
A parent with any open child, or with no children, is never proposed
The action has remote preconditions, a receipt, and is covered by tests
The sync skill no longer describes issue closure as out of scope for this case

items.title: Remove relationships the manifest no longer declares
items.description: When intent drops a parent or dependency, GitHub keeps showing it, so the board shows links the plan no longer has. Removing links the manifest no longer declares keeps the projection faithful without closing or deleting any issue. aio-agentic-sdlc's authority model currently cites 'never removes relationships' as satisfying one-way projection and must be amended in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: A sync plan proposes removing parent and dependency links that the manifest no longer declares, only between kit-managed issues
Each removal records what is needed to restore it
Links to issues outside the manifest are never removed
aio-agentic-sdlc doc/authority-model.md is amended to state the new boundary

items.title: Recognize Priority-only plans as pre-authorized
items.description: Owner decision 2026-09-24: a sync plan consisting solely of Priority field updates may be applied without a separate confirmation, like the release-workflow exception. Priority is derived by the kit and GitHub cannot compute it, so finished work otherwise keeps a stale score. The exemption must be checked by the engine, not by an agent reading the plan.
acceptance_criteria: The plan reports whether it contains only Priority field updates
sync-apply accepts such a plan without --confirm, and refuses any other plan without it
The plan is still bound to fresh state, verified after apply, and receipted
The sync skill documents the exemption and its limit

items.title: Preview unmanaged issues read-only
items.description: A read-only import preview lists unmanaged issues with inferred types and relationships, touching nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The preview performs no writes
Unselected issues are never modified

items.title: Assign stable IDs and apply adoption in deterministic batches
items.description: Reviewed mappings receive stable local IDs and are adopted in deterministic batches.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate mappings are rejected
A second import is idempotent

items.title: Cover adoption in the skills, not only the CLI
items.description:
The skills directory carries backlog-init, backlog-ingest, backlog-prioritize, backlog-sprint-plan and backlog-sync-github, and none of them mentions adoption. R11 and the relationship inference that followed it are reachable from the CLI and from docs/importing.md only.

That inverts the adoption story. An agent working through the installed plugin can initialize a backlog and synchronize one it already manages, but cannot take on a repository that already has issues, which is the path any new user is actually on. Ingestion handles one structured item at a time, so without an adoption skill the plugin's answer to an existing backlog is to re-file it by hand.

Found on 2026-09-21 while assessing readiness for use across existing projects.
acceptance_criteria: A skill covers the plan, review, apply and reconcile shape of adoption, including what adoption writes and what it leaves alone
It states that relationship inference is opt-in and why, and what a withheld relationship means
It routes orphan recovery to import-reconcile rather than to a second adoption
Skill structural validation and host manifest parity stay green

items.title: Recover an orphan with the structure GitHub records, not flat
items.description:
`import-reconcile` records a stranded marker under the id GitHub already uses, with neutral defaults and no relationships, even when GitHub records a parent and dependencies for that issue.

That is the divergence GH-63 removed from adoption, still present in the recovery path. Synchronization is additive and never removes a parent or a dependency, so a recovered item disagrees with its own repository permanently and silently. Adoption is now honest about structure and recovery is not.

Recovery is deliberately local and must stay that way: GitHub is already correct, so nothing here may write. Reading the parent and blocked-by set of the orphans being recovered is a read, and the same withholding rules that adoption uses apply unchanged.

Found on 2026-09-22 during the GH-63 live validation against aegolius-labs/abk-adopt-eval-20260922. See docs/adoption-live-validation-2026-09-22.md finding F2.
acceptance_criteria: Recovery proposes the parent and dependencies GitHub records for each orphan, under the same hierarchy and acyclic rules adoption uses
A relationship the manifest cannot express is withheld with its reason rather than forced
Recovery still writes nothing to GitHub
Reading relationships during recovery is opt-in on the same terms as adoption, so the default request cost is unchanged

items.title: Enforce the release baseline prerequisite without auto-tagging
items.description: Untagged release-bearing history silently analyzed zero commits before baseline setup (R14-F7). The prerequisite must be explicit and must not create a tag on its own.
acceptance_criteria: A missing baseline fails loudly
No tag is created automatically

items.title: Prove hosted recovery after draft creation and partial upload
items.description: Local recovery tests are insufficient; recovery must be demonstrated on a hosted run.
acceptance_criteria: A hosted run recovers from a partial asset upload

items.title: Compose fresh operational state for planning
items.description: Planning reads Status and Sprint from a fresh GitHub snapshot rather than from manifest intent.
acceptance_criteria: Planning inputs come from fresh remote state
Offline preview limits are documented

items.title: Preserve remote Status and Sprint during ordinary sync
items.description: An ordinary sync no longer writes Status or Sprint for existing managed items.
acceptance_criteria: Remote completion survives a sync with stale local intent
New items still receive manifest defaults

items.title: Represent operational changes as explicit digest-bound transitions
items.description: Changing Status or Sprint requires an explicit reviewed transition that fails closed on drift.
acceptance_criteria: A transition aborts when remote state moved since planning

items.title: Document legacy-manifest migration
items.description: Existing manifests carry operational intent that is no longer authoritative; document what changes for them.
acceptance_criteria: Migration guidance covers manifests written before D1

items.title: Account for retained target-sprint work exactly once
items.description: Capacity accounting counts work already committed to the target sprint once, without re-selecting it.
acceptance_criteria: Replanning does not double-count retained work

items.title: Offer explicit carryover review for work assigned elsewhere
items.description: Under carryover policy A, work assigned to another sprint is excluded from automatic selection and surfaced for explicit carryover.
acceptance_criteria: Work assigned elsewhere is never moved automatically
Carryover is presented for review

items.title: Refresh disposable resource identities before any cleanup plan
items.description: The prior receipt's identities are stale. Confirm absence of Project #4 and enumerate what actually remains.
acceptance_criteria: Remaining resources are enumerated from fresh discovery
No deletion is performed under this item

items.title: Delete the four retired evaluation resources under a confirmed plan
items.description: Delete abk-eval-wave-c-r02-20260827-gh-26c954aa-labels, abk-eval-wave-c-r02-20260827-api-3f546dc6-labels, Project #5, and abk-adopt-eval-20260922, each bound to the node ID recorded on 2026-09-24. Repository deletion needs a token with delete_repo, which the owner must grant; blocked until then.
acceptance_criteria: An identity-bound deletion plan is confirmed by digest before any deletion
Execution stops on the first failure without retry
Each resource is read back as absent
abk-release-eval-20260908 is untouched

items.title: Express the roadmap as a tracked manifest
items.description: Convert the roadmap's release lines and work items into a manifest the kit can manage.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest validates
Prioritization and sprint planning run

items.title: Scaffold and synchronize the kit's own Project
items.description: Drive scaffold and sync against the kit's own organization Project.
acceptance_criteria: A second sync plan contains zero actions

items.title: Write up first-use friction against the responsible item
items.description: Record every defect and awkwardness this exercise surfaces as evidence against the work item that owns it.
acceptance_criteria: Each observation names the item that owns it

items.title: Name the item and rejected field on apply failure
items.description: Carry the failing action's item id and payload into the error text the operator sees, not only into the receipt.
acceptance_criteria: The message names the item id
The message names the endpoint and rejected field

items.title: Explain an unavailable native issue type
items.description: When a native issue type is missing, say so and say which label was used instead, rather than reporting a bare validation failure.
acceptance_criteria: A missing native type is named
The label fallback actually taken is reported
